title: Vietnam school leaders' English requirements (2026)
description: What English Vietnam asks of principals and school leaders under Circular 94/2026, level by level, plus the 2018 principal standard and what it means for teachers.
h1: English requirements for school leaders in Vietnam: Circular 94/2026 and the principal standard
intro: From 19 December 2026, Vietnam's Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT counts a school as meeting Level 1 of the English-as-a-second-language framework only if at least one leader can work directly with foreigners in English; Level 3 needs two. The circular's reported wording names no certificate or CEFR level for leaders. The 2018 principal standard asked for everyday communication in a foreign language, with English preferred.
keyPoints: **Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT**, issued by the Ministry of Education and Training, was signed on 3 November 2026 and takes effect on 19 December 2026.

For general schools, Level 1 needs **at least one leader** who can work directly with foreigners in English. Level 3 needs **at least two**. Levels are cumulative, so Level 2 includes the Level 1 requirement.

No national English test, certificate or CEFR level for leaders appears in the official summaries or in the press reports of the circular. Each school judges itself through a self-assessment council, and its head is responsible for the result.
Self-assessment results may not be used to rank schools. For teachers, they may not be used directly for appraisal, appointment or recruitment unless another law says otherwise.

The older principal standard, Circular 14/2018/TT-BGDĐT, rated foreign-language use from everyday communication up to fluent use, with English preferred. Under Circular 30/2026/TT-BGDĐT, principals were assessed against it until the end of the 2025-2026 school year.

sections.title: What English do school leaders in Vietnam need?

blocks.text: There is no single English exam that every principal in Vietnam must pass. The new benchmark is **Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT** from the Ministry of Education and Training. It measures how far a school has gone in making English a second language, and one of its criteria is that the school's leaders can work with foreigners in English.

The circular puts into practice [Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/quyet-dinh-2371-qd-ttg-2025-phe-duyet-de-an-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-thu-hai-trong-truong-hoc-416990-d1.html) of 27 October 2025. That decision is the Prime Minister's approval of the national project to make English a second language in schools from 2025 to 2035, with a vision to 2045. According to the [Ministry of Education and Training's quality-assurance department](https://vqa.moet.gov.vn/vi/news/tin-tuc-su-kien/ban-hanh-tieu-chuan-tieu-chi-danh-gia-muc-do-trien-khai-de-an-dua-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-thu-hai-trong-truong-hoc-304.html), the circular was signed on 3 November 2026 and takes effect on 19 December 2026.

It has separate standards for preschools, general schools (primary, lower and upper secondary), continuing education, vocational education and universities, set out in Appendices I to V. The leader requirement that has been widely reported, and is quoted below, comes from **Appendix II, for general schools**.

blocks.title: Check the full text
blocks.text: Official summaries and press reports quote the leader criterion as a skill ("năng lực sử dụng tiếng Anh để làm việc trực tiếp với người nước ngoài"). None of them gives a CEFR level or names a certificate. Before you decide what evidence to file, read the appendices in the full text on [moet.gov.vn](https://moet.gov.vn/van-ban/van-ban-quy-pham-phap-luat/thong-tu-quy-dinh-tieu-chuan-tieu-chi-va-viec-danh-gia-muc-do-trien-khai-thuc-hien-de-an-dua-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-th.html?categoryId=101914860).

sections.title: What Circular 94/2026 asks of leaders and teachers, level by level

blocks.text: For general schools, Level 1 needs one English-capable leader and Level 3 needs two. Teachers who teach subject content in English must write a growing share of test content in English. The levels build on each other: a school reaches Level 2 only by meeting all of Level 1 plus the extra Level 2 requirements. If it does not fully meet Level 1, its level is "not determined".

blocks.caption: Appendix II (general schools) of Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT, as reported by LuatVietnam and Báo Văn hóa, November 2026
rows: Level 1
At least **one** leader can use English to work directly with foreigners
Enough English teachers, in number and language level, as the Ministry prescribes. Teachers who teach content in English can use English with foreigners as their duties require
Six standards in all, from the English-speaking environment to digital tools and AI
Level 2
No extra leader requirement reported, so the Level 1 requirement still applies
Content-in-English teachers meet the required language standards. At least **10%** of periodic test content in those subjects is in English (1 point out of 10)
Not detailed in the reports
Level 3
At least **two** leaders can work directly with foreigners in English
At least **50%** of periodic test content in English (5 points out of 10)
Organises at least **3** English activities a school year (clubs, contests, or exchanges with foreign partners or another Vietnamese school) and takes part in at least 3 more

blocks.text: These figures come from [LuatVietnam's summary of Appendix II](https://luatvietnam.vn/tin-van-ban-moi/hieu-truong-hoac-hieu-pho-truong-pho-thong-phai-biet-tieng-anh-de-lam-viec-voi-nguoi-nuoc-ngoai-186-115498-article.html) and from [Báo Văn hóa](https://baovanhoa.vn/truong-hoc-muon-dat-chuan-tieng-anh-muc-cao-lanh-dao-cung-can-nang-luc-ngoai-ngu.html), as of November 2026. [Vietbao](https://vietbao.vn/dua-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-thu-hai-hieu-truong-va-hieu-pho-can-dap-ung-gi-615332.html) also places the two-leader requirement at Level 3.

"Leader" means the school's leadership as a whole, not the principal alone. A vice principal who works in English can meet the Level 1 criterion. For vocational education, according to Báo Văn hóa, as of November 2026, the criterion is the share of managers at faculty, department, subject-group and centre level who meet the English requirement the institution itself sets: 50% to under 70% at Level 1, 70% to under 90% at Level 2 and at least 90% at Level 3. For the preschool and university appendices, the leader criteria were not in the reports, so read those appendices directly.

Each main campus, branch or teaching site counts as one unit. According to the [government's policy portal](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/tieu-chuan-danh-gia-muc-do-trien-khai-de-an-dua-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-thu-hai-trong-truong-hoc-119261110143301771.htm), as of November 2026, a school with three or more units needs at least 65% of them at a level to claim it. A school with fewer than three units needs every unit at that level. A chain with one English-capable deputy at head office should check whether that is enough for each site.

sections.title: How does a school prove its leaders meet the English requirement?

blocks.text: The school proves it itself. No outside body examines the leaders. The head of the school sets up a self-assessment council, compares the evidence with the criteria and signs off the level. The head is personally responsible for that decision, so the evidence for the leader criterion needs to stand up to inspection.

items.title: Set up the self-assessment council
items.text: The head of the school appoints the council (Hội đồng tự đánh giá).

items.title: Collect the evidence
items.text: The council gathers and analyses information, data and evidence. Records already held in the sector database or the school's own systems are reused and do not have to be submitted again.

items.title: Compare with the criteria
items.text: The council compares the school's current position with each criterion in the relevant appendix. According to the Ministry, results must be accurate and verifiable.

items.title: Recognise the level
items.text: When every requirement of a level is met, the head decides to recognise that level. A school may recognise a higher level as soon as it qualifies, without waiting for the project's review dates.

items.title: Publish and review every year
items.text: The result is updated in the education management information system and made public. Each year the school reviews its data and progress without repeating the whole self-assessment.

blocks.text: The process is set out by the [Ministry of Education and Training](https://vqa.moet.gov.vn/vi/news/tin-tuc-su-kien/ban-hanh-tieu-chuan-tieu-chi-danh-gia-muc-do-trien-khai-de-an-dua-tieng-anh-thanh-ngon-ngu-thu-hai-trong-truong-hoc-304.html). The same source says the school must provide the conditions and benefits the rules require for teachers who teach bilingually, and must fund teachers' English training where the law makes that training compulsory and funding it is the school's responsibility.

blocks.title: Results are not a league table
blocks.text: Self-assessment results may not be used to rank schools or to grade them in emulation (thi đua) ratings. For teachers, they may not be used directly for appraisal, appointment, recruitment or benefits unless another law provides otherwise.

sections.title: What does the principal standard say about English?

blocks.text: The professional standard for general-school principals, **Circular 14/2018/TT-BGDĐT**, has a foreign-language criterion (Criterion 17, under Standard 5 on languages and IT). It is rated at three levels, with English preferred. It assesses the principal personally, whereas Circular 94/2026 assesses the school.

blocks.caption: Foreign-language criterion in Circular 14/2018/TT-BGDĐT, as quoted by Giáo dục Việt Nam
rows: Pass (Đạt)
Everyday communication in a foreign language, English preferred
Good (Khá)
Direct the planning and delivery of a plan to build foreign-language skills among staff, teachers and students
Very good (Tốt)
Use a foreign language fluently, English preferred, and build an environment where others in the school develop theirs

blocks.text: The ratings are quoted in [Giáo dục Việt Nam](https://giaoduc.net.vn/yeu-cau-ngoai-ngu-trong-chuan-hieu-truong-chuan-giao-vien-xa-roi-thuc-te-post189685.gd). The status of the standard changed in 2026. Under Article 20(2) of [Circular 30/2026/TT-BGDĐT](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/circular-no-30-2026-tt-bgddt-dated-april-14-2026-of-ministry-of-education-and-training-providing-for-professional-standards-of-teachers-of-general-e-432094-doc1.html), in force since 14 April 2026, principals were assessed against Circular 14/2018 until the end of the 2025-2026 school year. The sources read for this guide do not confirm which standard replaces it from 2026-2027, so ask your provincial Department of Education and Training which one it now applies.

The same Circular 30/2026 requires general-school teachers to use foreign languages "as required by the job position" (Article 9 for primary teachers, Articles 12 and 15 for lower and upper secondary teachers). Leaders of universities and vocational institutions come under [Circular 17/2026/TT-BGDĐT](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/thong-tu-17-2026-tt-bgddt-tieu-chuan-lanh-dao-co-so-giao-duc-dai-hoc-va-nghe-nghiep-430557-d1.html), in force since 27 March 2026. Its standards for heads and deputy heads (Articles 2 to 6) do not mention a foreign language.

sections.title: How many schools in Vietnam are expected to reach each level?

blocks.text: The levels are national targets for a share of schools. They are not a deadline every school must meet. Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg sets the shares by period, and the first target is compulsory English from grade 1 in every general school.

blocks.caption: Targets for general schools in Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg (27 October 2025), as published by LuatVietnam
rows: At least 20% of general schools; compulsory English from grade 1 in 100% of general schools
At least 30%
At least 40%
At least 50%

blocks.text: The decision also includes training the English of school management staff, with priority for disadvantaged areas, and surveying the English of teachers who teach English or teach subjects in English. Staffing is the pressure point. According to [Nhân Dân](https://nhandan.vn/mot-lo-trinh-de-khong-ai-bi-bo-lai-post1000374.html), in a November 2026 article, Vietnam still needed about 22,000 English teachers as of early 2026, mainly in preschools and primary schools.

sections.title: What this means if you hire English teachers or look for schools in Vietnam

blocks.text: For a school leader, Level 1 depends on two things: one leader who can deal with foreigners in English, and enough qualified English teachers. Circular 94/2026 sets no separate rules for foreign teachers in the reports read for this guide. A foreign teacher's paperwork follows the usual work-permit and qualification rules.

items: For hiring a foreign teacher, including documents, work permit and timing, see [hiring a foreign English teacher in Vietnam](/guides/hire-a-foreign-english-teacher-in-vietnam) (in Vietnamese: [tuyển giáo viên nước ngoài](/huong-dan/tuyen-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-day-tieng-anh)).
For what a teacher needs to qualify, see [requirements to teach English in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/requirements-to-teach-english-in-vietnam).

For how bilingual and international schools differ from centres, see [types of English teaching jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/types-of-english-teaching-jobs-in-vietnam) and [international school jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).

blocks.text: If you are looking for schools near you in Ho Chi Minh City, start with [eno.vn's school directory](/schools). It lists language centres, international and bilingual schools, teacher agencies and universities. Teachers who worked or interviewed there can leave reviews, which a moderator reads before they appear, and the directory also shows open jobs. Most schools have few or no reviews yet, so treat it as a shortlist. Then ask each school directly about its English programme and whether it has self-assessed under Circular 94/2026.

faqs.q: What English level do school leaders in Vietnam need?
faqs.a: No CEFR level or certificate for school leaders appears in the reported text of Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT. The circular, issued by the Ministry of Education and Training and in force from 19 December 2026, asks that at least one general-school leader can work directly with foreigners in English for Level 1, and at least two for Level 3. Each school judges this through its own self-assessment council, and the head of the school is responsible for the result.

faqs.q: Do principals in Vietnam have to speak English?
faqs.a: Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT does not require every principal in Vietnam to speak English. It counts the school's leadership as a whole, so a vice principal who works in English can meet the Level 1 criterion. The older principal standard, Circular 14/2018/TT-BGDĐT, rated foreign-language use from everyday communication up to fluent use, with English preferred. Circular 30/2026 kept that standard for assessing principals until the end of the 2025-2026 school year.

Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT was signed by Vietnam's Ministry of Education and Training on 3 November 2026 and takes effect on 19 December 2026. Circular 94/2026 sets three cumulative levels and a self-assessment process for schools carrying out Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg, the national project to make English a second language in schools from 2025 to 2035. Separate appendices cover preschools, general schools, continuing education, vocational education and universities.

faqs.q: Is English compulsory from grade 1 in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Decision 2371/QĐ-TTg of 27 October 2025 sets a 2025-2030 target that 100% of general schools in Vietnam teach compulsory English from grade 1. Decision 2371 is the Prime Minister's approval of the project to make English a second language in schools. When a particular school starts compulsory English from grade 1 depends on local implementation, so parents should ask the school or the local education authority.

faqs.q: Are Circular 94 results used to rank schools in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Self-assessment results under Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT may not be used to rank or classify schools in Vietnam, or as a direct basis for emulation ratings. For teachers, the results may not be used directly for appraisal, appointment, recruitment or benefits unless another law provides otherwise. Schools update their recognised level in the education management information system and make it public, then review their progress every year.

faqs.q: Do university leaders in Vietnam need a foreign language?
faqs.a: Circular 17/2026/TT-BGDĐT sets the standards for heads and deputy heads of universities and vocational institutions in Vietnam. It was signed and took effect on 27 March 2026. Its standards in Articles 2 to 6 do not mention a foreign language. Universities still come under Circular 94/2026/TT-BGDĐT, which has a separate appendix for higher education within the English-as-a-second-language framework.

faqs.q: Where can I find schools in Vietnam near me?
faqs.a: In Ho Chi Minh City, eno.vn's school directory lists language centres, international schools, bilingual schools, teacher agencies and universities. It also shows open jobs and reviews from teachers who worked or interviewed there. Most schools in the directory have few or no reviews yet, so use it as a shortlist. Ask each school directly about its English programme, its teachers and whether it has self-assessed under Circular 94/2026.
